saints.name: Sts. Cyril and Methodius
saints.title: Bishop and Monk
saints.shortBlurb: Brothers of Thessalonica, apostles of the Slavs, who gave them an alphabet and the liturgy in their own tongue…
biography: The brothers were Greeks of Thessalonica: Methodius, born about 815, a governor turned monk, and Constantine, born about 827, a priest and philosopher. Sent first to the Khazars, they were called in 863 to Great Moravia, whose prince Rastislav had asked the Emperor Michael III for teachers in the Slavic tongue.

Constantine devised an alphabet for the Slavs, called Glagolitic, and with his brother translated the Scriptures and the liturgy — a work the Frankish clergy opposed, holding that God might be worshipped only in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin. The brothers carried their cause to Rome, where Pope Hadrian II approved the Slavonic liturgy.

Constantine, now a monk under the name Cyril, died at Rome on 14 February 869 and was buried at San Clemente. Methodius, made archbishop and legate to the Slavs, laboured on despite two years and a half in a Swabian prison, until his death on 6 April 885; his funeral was sung in Greek, Latin, and Slavonic.

Their disciples, driven out of Moravia, carried the Slavonic liturgy to Bulgaria; the Cyrillic alphabet, named for Cyril, descends from their work. In 1980 Pope John Paul II declared the two brothers, with Benedict, co-patrons of Europe.
saints.knownFor: Bringing the Gospel, letters, and liturgy to the Slavic peoples.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; co-patrons of Europe (1980)

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 14 February
